objectClass.primaryType: single-storey branded retail building shell (Makro livery)
objectClass.notes: Exterior shell only, by design: a level-builder prop is only ever seen from outside, so no interior geometry is authored and the shopfront glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane rather than an aperture. The shell is bilaterally symmetric front-to-back; the fenestration is not, since the roller service shutter appears on the right side wall alone.

reasoning: Silhouette scores 1 of 3: the shape is a single cuboid and carries almost none of the identity.

Identity lives in surface organisation and repeated detail instead -- the mullion rhythm, the cladding rib pitch, the roof plant cluster -- so repetitionDensity, materialLayerCount and localDetailDensity all score 3 of 3, and they are what set the tier at complex.
occlusionRisk 6: the single high three-quarter view hides the rear and left elevations entirely and the parapet crops the roof plant.
actionReadinessNeed scores 0 of 3: the prop is a static rigid body and nothing on it articulates.
The binding budget axis at hero2x is uniqueGeometries (8), not triangles (16000). The component count is therefore chosen in the blockout, not trimmed later.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Complex from observed structure: seven material layers, four repetition systems and six micro feature groups on a trivially simple silhouette. Repetition systems are mandatory here because the uniqueGeometries ceiling is 8 - the mullion rhythm and the roof plant cannot exist as componentTree parts at all within that budget.

details.description: Red lowercase makro wordmark with a thin light outline, centred on the banner over about 46% of its width.
Lighter-blue folded return around the sign tray.
Vertical trapezoidal ribs at 0.25 m pitch on the blue front cladding. DEFERRED to the reserved draw call: an XY elevation extruded along Z cannot express relief along Z.
The same rib profile on the white side and rear walls, authored into the shell's castellated plan profile.
Lighter UNRIBBED coping cap running the whole parapet perimeter, proud of both faces.
Six mullions dividing eight 0.84 m bays under a high transom rail.
Centre entrance pair with a lowered head, a meeting stile and a slim pull handle.
Blue front fascia edge and underside under a pale concrete top slab.
The tight specular lobe that makes the pane read as glass rather than a hole.
Horizontal slat ribs on the roller shutter, recessed in a proud surround.
Circular fan cowls above each condenser body.
Dark mounting feet under each condenser body.
Low rectangular duct runs along the right and rear of the deck.
Concrete kerb standing proud around the base; it defines the module's x and -z faces.

Blue cladding RETURN at the two front arrises. Recorded as white flat trim at blockout; the structural-pass sheet shows the plate wraps both front corners in the same blue as the facade, so the two instances moved from white-trim to blue-trim. They do not break the rib run -- the ribs stop 0.15 m short of them.
Vertical run-off streaking below the coping drip, heaviest at the corners.

Each was closed by adopting an explicit assumption with its basis and confidence; those five records are carried verbatim in spec.assumptions and in full in spec.unknownsDetail, and the two weakest -- the rear elevation at 0.55 and the left elevation at 0.60 -- are also carried as a `hidden-elevations` risk and reported to the user. No coincident co-facing surfaces: check-coplanar.mjs exits 0.
All four budget ceilings hold as MEASURED off the built model, not estimated.

qualityContract.mesoDepthNote: Set to 2, the number of meso COMPONENT MESHES this prop can afford, and lowered with reason rather than to silence a warning. Only fascia-banner and entrance-canopy are meso meshes; shopfront-glazing was reclassified MACRO because a 6.74 m opening in an 8.0 m elevation is the building's mass, not detail applied to it. pivots.name: Root pivot
pivots.notes: The declared asset pivot is base-center and this is the ONLY pivot on the prop. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on that axis, and nothing on this building turns.

actionReadiness.socketsNote: ZERO sockets, deliberately. A named socket is a promise that something attaches there, and nothing attaches to this prop. Naming markers after places on the surface -- socket-fascia-front, socket-roof-center -- would describe a machine that does not exist.
actionReadiness.rollerShutterNote: The roller service shutter was CONSIDERED as an articulating part and rejected. Modelling it as a moving element would need a `shutter-roll` pivot at its head roll axis AND a recess behind it for the slats to roll into -- which is interior geometry, which this prop does not have by design. A shutter that opens onto a solid wall is a worse promise than a shutter that is plainly closed. It ships as a fixed closed panel and this spec says so.
actionReadiness.partCoverageNote: Every component and every repetition system is a named, separately addressable node under root.

componentTree.name: Side and rear wall shell with parapet
componentTree.topologyRationale: A U-shaped footprint ring extruded 4.12 m upward: the -X, rear and +X walls at 0.20 m thickness, open on +Z where the facade wall takes over. Hollow by construction, which is the whole point -- this is an exterior shell and there is no interior to draw. The parapet is the same extrusion continuing past the roof deck at 3.50 m rather than a separate proud element, because the plate shows one unbroken corrugated surface from kerb to coping.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: U-plan ring, 0.20 m walls, extruded to y=4.12. The OUTER edge is castellated at 0.25 m pitch and 0.03 m relief to author the vertical rib profile of the cladding as real geometry.

ribProfile.evidence: heightP90Gradient 0.18566 on material-crops/white-cladding.png, the highest relief signal measured anywhere on this plate. Bought with triangles (about 1400 of 16000), which are the axis with headroom, and costing ZERO draw calls, geometries and materials -- the three axes that are at or near their ceiling.
ribProfile.innerEdgeNote: Only the OUTER loop is ribbed. The inner loop stays a plain rectangle: it faces a cavity nobody sees, and ribbing it would triple the cap triangulation for nothing.

geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: 238 outer profile points (castellated) plus 4 inner, one extrusion step: about 1400 triangles including both caps.
geometryDescriptor.shapeSpaceNote: Profile is authored in (sx, sy) = (worldX, -worldZ). The component carries rotationEuler [-pi/2, 0, 0], mapping the shape plane onto the ground plane and the extrusion axis onto world +Y. Extrude components are NOT unit-scaled by the generator, so these are the building's actual footprint coordinates in metres.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The U's open ends stop at sy=-2.70, which is worldZ=+2.70 -- the facade wall's BACK face -- not at +2.90 where its front face is. Two surfaces in the same plane facing the SAME direction tear into interleaved triangles as the camera moves; this joint is instead a butt of OPPOSED faces, which is how solids are meant to meet.
geometryDescriptor.copingHandoffNote: The walls stop at y=4.12 and the parapet COPING owns 4.04..4.20. The wall's top face is BURIED inside the coping span and only the coping's own top is exposed, so there is no pair of coincident +Y faces. Overall height is set by the roof plant at 4.60, not by the parapet.
geometryDescriptor.scaleConvention: NO `scale` key on transform, deliberately. generate_threejs_factory.py's scale_vector() SHORT-CIRCUITS on the presence of transform.scale and returns it verbatim; only when the key is ABSENT does it fall through to sizing the unit box from dimensions.width/height/depth. An authored `scale: [1, 1, 1]` therefore reads as 'this box is one metre cubed', and every box in a first draft of this spec collapsed to a unit cube -- the roof deck rendered as a 1 m box. The extrude components are the exact opposite and MUST KEEP scale: [1, 1, 1]: their profile2D points are already in real metres, so falling through to dimensions would rescale an 8 m building by a further 8 x 4.6 x 7.
geometryDescriptor.rotationKeyNote: The generator reads transform.ROTATION, not transform.rotationEuler. A first draft carried -pi/2 in rotationEuler alone and rotation [0,0,0] beside it; the generated factory wrote rotation.set(0,0,0) and extruded the U-plan along +Z instead of +Y, so the footprint became an elevation and 2.50 m of wall hung below ground. Both keys are now written and kept equal.

collider.notes: The declared asset collider is `box`. ONE convex box proxy spanning the whole declared module, ROOT-relative: x -4.00..4.00, y 0..4.60, z -3.50..3.50. Nothing else carries a collider -- a player collides with the building, and the canopy and roof plant sit inside this box's span. promote-model.mjs requires at least one collider on a prop whose declared collider is not `none`. The offset's z was -0.45 for five passes, which is exactly the PRE-REFINE shell centre (-3.40 + 2.50) / 2: authored before the depth refine moved the facade front to +2.90 and never re-registered, so the proxy stood 0.45 m proud of the rear wall and stopped 0.95 m short of the canopy. Same root cause as the hand tail's placement drift, and invisible for the same reason -- a collider renders nothing, so no comparison sheet could show it.

actionProfile.colliderNote: The declared asset collider is `box`. The shell carries it as the whole prop's physics proxy in its own local frame; nothing else needs one, since a convex box around the building is what a player collides with and the canopy and plant sit inside its span.

surfaceDetail.locality: Profiled steel sheet: rib crowns catch the key and read glossier than the valleys, which is a geometric effect of the castellation rather than a roughness variation.
surfaceDetail.note: bumpAmplitude is 0 by design, not by omission. Every relief on this prop is carried as GEOMETRY -- the shell's rib castellation in its plan profile, the blue-trim parapet ribs, the condenser louvres and the shutter slats -- and all eight materials are declared textureless with evidence, so a bump or normal channel here would both contradict that declaration and re-introduce the procedural texture synthesis those declarations exist to skip. What this block carries is roughness LOCALITY, which is real and map-free.

componentTree.name: Blue front elevation with shopfront opening
componentTree.topologyRationale: A Shape WITH A HOLE, extruded 0.20 m in +Z. This is the one part of the shell a plan extrusion cannot express, because the shopfront opening is a vertical void: the front wall is therefore authored in elevation instead of in plan. It costs one draw call and one geometry and it buys the blue-front / white-return split that is the prop's second identity feature.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front elevation in the XY plane extruded 0.20 m along +Z: an outer rectangle 7.80 x 4.12 m with one rectangular hole for the shopfront. Piers of 0.53 m survive at each end, which the plate shows as blue cladding returning past the glazing.
geometryDescriptor.segmentRationale: Four outline points and four hole points, one extrusion step: about 120 triangles including the reveal faces.
geometryDescriptor.shapeSpaceNote: Authored in (sx, sy) = (worldX, worldY) with no rotation; the extrusion axis is world +Z, spanning z=+2.50 to z=+2.70.
geometryDescriptor.ribNote: The vertical rib relief the plate shows on this blue face is NOT authored here: a shape extruded along Z from an XY elevation cannot express ribs whose relief is along Z. It was the one deliberately deferred item in the blockout, held for the prop's spare draw call until a render showed the front reading too flat beside the ribbed sides. The structural-pass sheet was that render, and the `blue-trim` system now carries it: 30 ribs at the shell's own 0.25 m pitch across the parapet band (y=3.70..4.04), standing 0.025 m proud of this wall's FRONT face at z=+2.90. It spends the twelfth and last draw call and nothing else -- it reuses the shared unit box and this component's own `blue-cladding` material, so unique geometries stay at 8 and materials at 8. The same cluster carries the two front corner returns, which the plate shows as blue cladding wrapping both corners rather than the white flashing the blockout invented for them.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The opening's four reveal faces are the classic z-fighting trap: a frame whose hole is EXACTLY the wall's opening puts four coincident co-facing faces in the model. Nothing in this prop meets those reveals. The glazing pane is inset to z=+2.545..2.585 and OVERSIZED to +-3.44 x 0.09..2.49, so it passes BEHIND the reveal rather than meeting it; the framing cluster overlaps the opening edge by 0.06 m on all four sides and stands proud to z=+2.73, clear of the wall's own front face at +2.70.

An authored `scale: [1, 1, 1]` therefore reads as 'this box is one metre cubed', and every box in a first draft of this spec collapsed to a unit cube -- the roof deck rendered as a 1 m box. The extrude components are the exact opposite and MUST KEEP scale: [1, 1, 1]: their profile2D points are already in real metres, so falling through to dimensions would rescale an 8 m building by a further 8 x 4.6 x 7.
geometryDescriptor.frontFaceNote: This wall's front face is at z=+2.90, not +2.70: the depth refine moved the facade forward 0.20 m. Every hand-authored instance that references the front face -- shopfront framing, coping front, kerb front, canopy top slab, corner returns, parapet ribs -- must be measured from +2.90. They were not, for one pass: authored against the old +2.70 they sat BEHIND this wall and drew nothing, which is a failure that renders as a clean image rather than as an error.

repetitionSystems.name: Shopfront framing, mullions and transoms
repetitionSystems.rationale: Perimeter frame, six mullions dividing eight 0.84 m bays, a high transom rail, the centre pair's lowered head and meeting stile, and its pull handle. Fourteen boxes for ONE draw call and ZERO unique geometries. As componentTree parts they would be fourteen of each, on a prop whose entire ceiling is eight geometries -- this system is not an optimisation, it is the only way the bay rhythm fits the budget at all.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: Every framing member that CROSSES another has its OWN front and back plane, staggered in the order a real frame is built: jambs proudest at z=2.736, then head and sill rails at 2.728, the transom at 2.718, the mullions at 2.710, the door stile at 2.714 and the door head at 2.706. Two members in the same plane facing the same way would tear into interleaved triangles exactly where they cross, which is the most visible place on the prop. Members that never cross -- the six mullions -- do share a plane, which is harmless because they do not overlap in x. The whole band stands proud of the wall's front face at +2.70 and none of it lands ON 2.700. Backs are staggered 2.588..2.604, clear of the glazing's front face at +2.585.

repetitionSystems.name: Parapet coping and shutter surround
repetitionSystems.rationale: One material and one draw call for every piece of white folded flashing on the prop. The coping is the identity edge -- a continuous light cap line around the whole parapet -- and the plate shows the same flashing returning as corner trim at the two front arrises and as the surround the roller shutter sits inside.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The four coping bars BUTT end to end rather than overlapping: the side bars span z=-3.30..+2.45 and stop where the front and rear bars begin, so no two coping tops share the y=4.20 plane. Had they overlapped at the corners, the overlapping region would have put two +Y faces in the same plane facing the same way. Coping and flashing both stand 0.10 m proud of the wall faces they cap; the flashing stops at y=3.90, short of the wall top at 4.12, so it shares no plane with it.

repetitionSystems.name: Base kerb and canopy top slab
repetitionSystems.rationale: The base kerb's four bars and the canopy's pale top surface are the same precast concrete, so they are one InstancedMesh. performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The binding axis is unique geometries, not triangles: the generator bakes each component's real dimensions into vertex data via geometry.scale(), so every componentTree box is a genuinely distinct geometry however similar it looks. The tree was therefore designed to the ceiling IN THE BLOCKOUT -- six component geometries plus a shared unit box and a shared unit cylinder -- rather than optimised into it at the end. That ordering matters: a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Six meshes and five InstancedMeshes. ONE draw call is left deliberately unspent, reserved for a `blue-trim` system carrying the vertical rib relief on the blue front, which the shell's plan-profile rib trick cannot reach. It is held back until a render shows the front reading too flat beside the ribbed sides -- adding a repetitionSystem later is safe because it does not restructure components.

materials.note: At the ceiling with no headroom. blue-cladding is shared by the facade wall and the entrance canopy; concrete-grey by the roof deck, the base kerb and the canopy top slab; galvanised by the roof plant and the roller shutter. The red wordmark is a canvas REGION on the sign-blue material, not a material of its own -- a colour difference is not a material difference. trim-white is the eighth and it earns its slot on an observable difference from white-cladding: the coping is UNRIBBED where the wall it caps is ribbed.

uniqueGeometries.note: Six component geometries (two extrusions, four boxes) plus ONE unit BoxGeometry shared by four clusters and ONE unit CylinderGeometry shared by the fan cowls; the clusters carry their sizes in per-instance matrices. This axis is at its ceiling with zero headroom and is the binding constraint on the prop. VALIDATOR CAVEAT: validate_sculpt_spec.py models unique geometries as len(components) + len(repetitionSystems), which is true of its own radial emitter and false of these hand-emitted clusters; it will read 11. The measured truth is 8, and render-model.mjs measures it off the built model.

triangles.note: About 15% of the triangle ceiling. Triangles are emphatically NOT the binding constraint -- unique geometries and materials are, both at their ceiling. The largest single item is the shell's castellated plan profile at roughly 1430 triangles, and that is the point: rib relief is bought on the axis with 13,600 triangles of headroom instead of on the three axes that have none. The remaining headroom is available for more silhouette work and must NOT be read as an invitation to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

timeToFirstDraw.note: All EIGHT materials declare textureless, so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely. Eight materials at 1024 would have cost roughly 15 s of pixel-by-pixel canvas writing inside createObjectModel before the drawer could show anything. The one canvas this prop does build -- the makro wordmark -- is assigned AFTER material construction and is unaffected.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: Read off the plate's shading split: the +Z front and the +X side both carry light with the front marginally brighter, and the roof deck is the brightest plane, so the key is high and forward of the right shoulder. Shadow edges under the canopy are soft, so it is a broad source.
The plate is a flat studio cut-out with no cast shadow and no ground plane; unlit faces sit only about 20% below lit ones, which is a strong ambient fill rather than a second lamp.

contactShadow.note: Contact/ground shadow is authored as a CONTRACT for the host scene, not baked: the plate is a studio cut-out with no ground plane, so there is no measured contact shadow to copy. A floor-placed building needs a grounding shadow where the kerb meets the ground or it reads as hovering.

ambientOcclusion.note: Ambient occlusion at the canopy soffit, the shopfront reveals, the shutter recess and under the coping drip -- the four places this prop has real cavities. AO is a lighting response here and is NOT written into any base colour.

lightingFromPhoto.evidence: A cool separation edge along the parapet coping and the front-right corner arris, which is what keeps the white coping legible against the white wall below it.

lightingFromPhoto.note: Low, and deliberately. The review harness has no environment map, which is exactly why aluminium and galvanised carry reduced metalness -- a metal near 1 with nothing to reflect renders near-black.

exposure.note: ACES filmic tone mapping at exposure 1.0, matching the render harness so the review comparison is like for like.

Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
